examples: The rope is slack.
The sail was slack.
The line went slack.

more.def: Not pulled tight, or loose.
examples: The rope hung slack between the posts.
The sail was slack with no wind.
The fishing line went slack.

easy.def: To shut with a loud bang.
examples: The door slammed.
He slammed the door.
The wind slams the gate.

more.def: To shut or hit something hard so that it makes a loud noise.
examples: The wind slammed the door shut.
Please do not slam the car door.
He slammed the book on the desk.

easy.def: To hit something with a flat hand.
examples: I slap the water.
He slapped a mosquito.
The wave slapped the boat.

more.def: To hit something with the flat of your hand, with a sharp sound.
examples: She slapped the water to make a splash.
He slapped the mosquito on his arm.
The waves slapped against the side of the boat.

easy.def: A person who is owned by another and must work for free.
examples: Long ago, many slaves worked on farms.
Slavery was cruel and unfair.
The book tells about a slave who ran to freedom.

more.def: A person who was treated as property and forced to work without freedom or pay.
examples: Harriet Tubman helped many slaves escape to freedom.
In the past, slaves were bought and sold, which was wrong and cruel.
Our class read a story about a slave who learned to read in secret.

easy.def: To rest with your eyes closed.
examples: I sleep at night.
The baby is sleeping.
The cat slept all day.

more.def: To rest your body and mind with your eyes closed, as you do at night.
examples: Bears sleep through most of the winter.
I slept well after the long hike.
Please be quiet because the baby is sleeping.

easy.def: The rest you get at night.
examples: I need sleep.
She got a good sleep.
He fell into a deep sleep.

more.def: The natural rest that your body needs every night.
examples: Children need a lot of sleep to grow and learn.
I fell into a deep sleep as soon as my head touched the pillow.
A good night of sleep helps you feel ready for school.
I am sleepy.
The sleepy baby yawned.
She felt sleepy.

more.def: Feeling tired and ready to go to sleep.
examples: The baby was sleepy after her bath.
I felt sleepy after the long car ride.
The sleepy puppy curled up in its bed.

easy.def: The part of a shirt that covers your arm.
examples: The sleeve is long.
I rolled up my sleeve.
My sleeve is torn.

more.def: The part of a piece of clothing that covers your arm.
examples: I rolled up my sleeves to wash dishes.
The sleeve of his coat was torn.
She wiped her nose on her sleeve.

easy.def: A thin, flat piece cut from something.
examples: I ate a slice of pizza.
The slice of bread is thin.
I want a slice of cake.

more.def: A thin, flat piece that has been cut from something larger.
examples: She cut a thin slice of ham for the sandwich.
Dad put a slice of cheese on the bread.
She cut a slice of watermelon.
I slice the apple.
She sliced the bread.
Please slice the tomato.

more.def: To cut something into thin, flat pieces.
examples: Mom sliced the bread for sandwiches.
He sliced the apple into eight pieces.
The chef sliced the tomatoes.
The road is slick.
The ice is slick.
The floor was slick.

more.def: Smooth and wet so that it is slippery.
examples: The road was slick with rain.
The floor was slick, so I walked carefully.
Slick ice covered the steps.

easy.def: To move smoothly over a surface.
examples: I slide on the ice.
The sled slides down the hill.
He slid on the floor.

more.def: To move smoothly and quietly along a surface.
examples: The kids slid down the snowy hill on sleds.
The drawer slides open easily.
He slid across the floor in his socks.

easy.def: A smooth, slanted toy that you go down.
examples: I go down the slide.
The slide is fun.
We played on the slide.

more.def: A smooth, slanted play structure that children climb up and come down on.
examples: The children took turns on the slide at the park.
The slide is so tall that you can see the whole playground.
The little girl climbed the ladder and zoomed down the slide.
There was a slight breeze.
A slight change is fine.
I felt a slight pain.

more.def: Small in size or amount.
examples: A slight breeze moved the curtains.
There is a slight chance of rain.
She felt a slight pain in her toe.
I am slightly tired.
The door was slightly open.
It is slightly cold.

more.def: To a small degree.
examples: He was slightly late for school.
I felt slightly sick after eating too fast.
The soup was slightly too salty.
The slim tree sways.
She has a slim book.
The slim bike is fast.

more.def: Thin and narrow.
examples: The slim tree swayed in the wind.
She tucked a slim book into her bag.
The path between the two walls was slim.
Do not slip on the ice.
He slipped on the wet floor.
The soap slipped from my hand.

more.def: To slide by accident and almost fall, or to slide out of place.
examples: Be careful not to slip on the icy steps.
The cup slipped out of my wet hands.
She slipped on a banana peel in the cartoon.
She slipped out the door.
The cat slipped into the room.
He slipped away.

more.def: To move quietly or without being noticed.
examples: The cat slipped through the open door.
She slipped a note into his bag.
We slipped out of the room as the baby slept.

easy.def: A soft shoe you wear indoors.
examples: I wear slippers at home.
The slipper is warm.
My slippers are fuzzy.

more.def: A soft, light shoe that is worn indoors.
examples: I wear my slippers around the house.
Her slippers were warm and fuzzy.
The dog chewed my slipper.

easy.def: So wet or smooth that you might slide.
examples: The ice is slippery.
The wet floor is slippery.
A fish is slippery to hold.

more.def: So smooth, wet, or icy that it is hard to hold or walk on.
examples: Be careful, because the floor is slippery when it is wet.
The soap was too slippery to hold.
Wet leaves made the sidewalk slippery.
His handwriting is sloppy.
A sloppy job.
The sloppy sandwich fell apart.

more.def: Done in a careless way, or messy and wet.
examples: His handwriting was sloppy and hard to read.
The sloppy painter got paint on the floor.
The sandwich was so sloppy it dripped.
Put a coin in the slot.
The slot is thin.
Drop the letter in the slot.

more.def: A narrow opening or space that something fits into.
examples: Slide your ticket into the slot at the gate.
The mail drops through a slot in the door.
The card fits into the slot.
A snail is slow.
The slow bus is late.
The turtle is slow.

more.def: Moving or happening at a low speed, or taking a long time.
examples: The snail made slow progress across the garden.
We were stuck behind a slow truck.
The line at the store was slow.
Slow down, please.
The bus slowed at the corner.
Cars slow near the school.

more.def: To lower the speed of something, or to move at a lower speed.
examples: The driver slowed the car at the crosswalk.
Please slow down before the corner.
Rain slowed the runners.
The turtle walks slowly.
Eat slowly.
Please speak slowly.

more.def: At a slow speed, taking a long time.
examples: The snail crept slowly across the path.
He slowly opened the door so it would not squeak.
Read the directions slowly and carefully.

easy.def: A slimy animal with no shell.
examples: A slug is on the leaf.
The slug is slow.
Slugs leave a trail.

more.def: A soft, slimy, crawling animal like a snail but with no shell.
examples: A slug left a shiny trail on the leaf.
Slugs eat plants in the garden.
The slug was gray and slimy.
